results.note: Matches the stated places: residents dying in the US, the four code ranges (X85 'homicide'), acute-intoxication basis, both exclusions, certifier, three literal-text fields, assumed involvement unless context says otherwise, T40.4 and T40.2 groupings (oxycodone 'generally' T40.2).

3rd paragraph: certifiers complete the certificate, NCHS codes it with automating software. 4th paragraph: named opioid analgesic T40.2-T40.4, 'opioid' alone T40.6, 'drug overdose' T50.9 with the opioid not reflected in coding. Exact.

results.corrected_extracted: The national programme on Substance Abuse Deaths (np-SAD), fed by coroners, supplied local performance figures under a wider definition than the UK Drug Strategy definition, also counting deaths in which psychoactive substances were implicated (with or without a post-mortem), deaths with a history of drug use problems and deaths with controlled drugs present at post-mortem. Of the 70 deaths np-SAD reported for Liverpool (57 deaths in 2004 and 28 inquests in January to June 2005, duplicates removed), np-SAD placed 38 in its category for people with a known history of problem drug use, 21 outside it and 11 as unknown; 45 were deaths from drug toxicity (prescribed drugs included) and 55 were of Liverpool residents. Editors' arithmetic: 25 of the 70 were not deaths from drug toxicity and 15 were not Liverpool residents.
results.note: Moved: 'with or without a post-mortem' belongs to 'substances implicated' (Background, 2nd paragraph), not to 'controlled drugs present at post-mortem'. All counts confirmed in Table 1 (70-45 = 25; 70-55 = 15). 'Fed by coroners' is inferred from np-SAD's criteria.

Bullet 'Attribution to a specific drug' after the 3rd paragraph: morphine mentions could refer to heroin, which could understate heroin and overstate morphine deaths. NCHS states a possibility, not a measured bias; the anchor keeps it conditional.

2nd paragraph, citing ref. 2 (Warner et al., 2013): 92%, 62%, 73%, 71% as stated. The commentary cites rather than quotes; the figures are averages across states ('on average'), with no years, counts or adjustment given.
